verses.original: וַיְהִ֗י כְּכַלֹּתוֹ֙ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל וְנֶ֙פֶשׁ֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן נִקְשְׁרָ֖ה בְּנֶ֣פֶשׁ דָּוִ֑ד וַיֶּאֱהָבוֹ יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן כְּנַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî kə·ḵal·lō·ṯōw lə·ḏab·bêr ’el- šā·’ūl wə·ne·p̄eš yə·hō·w·nā·ṯān niq·šə·rāh bə·ne·p̄eš dā·wiḏ way·yɛ·ʾɛ̆·hå̄·ḇō yə·hō·w·nā·ṯān kə·nap̄·šōw
verses.literal: After David had finished speaking with Saul the souls of Jonathan and David were knit together . . . and Jonathan loved him as himself
verses.literalPt: E SUCEDEU que, acabando ele de falar com Saul, a alma de Jônatas se ligou com a alma de Davi; e Jônatas o amou, como à sua própria alma.

verses.original: וַיִּקָּחֵ֥הוּ שָׁא֖וּל בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְלֹ֣א נְתָנ֔וֹ לָשׁ֖וּב בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיו׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiq·qā·ḥê·hū šā·’ūl bay·yō·wm ha·hū wə·lō nə·ṯā·nōw lā·šūḇ bêṯ ’ā·ḇîw
verses.literal: And from that day Saul kept David with him and did not let him return to his father’s house
verses.literalPt: E Saul naquele dia o tomou, e não lhe permitiu que voltasse para casa de seu pai.

verses.original: וַיִּכְרֹ֧ת יְהוֹנָתָ֛ן וְדָוִ֖ד בְּרִ֑ית בְּאַהֲבָת֥וֹ אֹת֖וֹ כְּנַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiḵ·rōṯ yə·hō·w·nā·ṯān wə·ḏā·wiḏ bə·rîṯ bə·’a·hă·ḇā·ṯōw ’ō·ṯōw kə·nap̄·šōw
verses.literal: Then Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as himself
verses.literalPt: E Jônatas e Davi fizeram aliança; porque Jônatas o amava como à sua própria alma.

verses.original: וַיִּתְפַּשֵּׁ֣ט יְהוֹנָתָ֗ן אֶֽת־ הַמְּעִיל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֔יו וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖הוּ לְדָוִ֑ד וּמַדָּ֕יו וְעַד־ חַרְבּ֥וֹ וְעַד־ קַשְׁתּ֖וֹ וְעַד־ חֲגֹרֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiṯ·paš·šêṭ yə·hō·w·nā·ṯān ’eṯ- ham·mə·‘îl ’ă·šer ‘ā·lāw way·yit·tə·nê·hū lə·ḏā·wiḏ ū·mad·dāw wə·‘aḏ- ḥar·bōw wə·‘aḏ- qaš·tōw wə·‘aḏ- ḥă·ḡō·rōw
verses.literal: And Jonathan removed the robe he was wearing and gave it to David along with his tunic . . . his sword . . . his bow . . . and his belt
verses.literalPt: E Jônatas se despojou da capa que trazia sobre si, e a deu a Davi, como também as suas vestes, até a sua espada, e o seu arco, e o seu cinto.

verses.original: וַיֵּצֵ֨א דָוִ֜ד בְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁלָחֶ֤נּוּ שָׁאוּל֙ יַשְׂכִּ֔יל וַיְשִׂמֵ֣הוּ שָׁא֔וּל עַ֖ל אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיִּיטַב֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י כָל־ הָעָ֔ם וְגַ֕ם בְּעֵינֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֥י שָׁאֽוּל׃פ
verses.transliteration: way·yê·ṣê ḏā·wiḏ bə·ḵōl ’ă·šer yiš·lā·ḥen·nū šā·’ūl yaś·kîl way·śi·mê·hū šā·’ūl ‘al ’an·šê ham·mil·ḥā·māh way·yî·ṭaḇ bə·‘ê·nê ḵāl hā·‘ām wə·ḡam bə·‘ê·nê ‘aḇ·ḏê šā·’ūl
verses.literal: So David marched out and prospered in everything Saul sent him to do and Saul set him over the men of war And this was pleasing in the sight of all the people and of Saul’s officers as well . . .
verses.literalPt: E saía Davi aonde quer que Saul o enviasse e conduzia-se com prudência, e Saul o pôs sobre os homens de guerra; e era aceito aos olhos de todo o povo, e até aos olhos dos servos de Saul.

verses.original: וַיְהִ֣י בְּבוֹאָ֗ם בְּשׁ֤וּב דָּוִד֙ מֵהַכּ֣וֹת אֶת־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י וַתֵּצֶ֨אנָה הַנָּשִׁ֜ים מִכָּל־ עָרֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לָשׁוּר וְהַמְּחֹל֔וֹת לִקְרַ֖את שָׁא֣וּל הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ בְּתֻפִּ֥ים בְּשִׂמְחָ֖ה וּבְשָׁלִשִֽׁים׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî bə·ḇō·w·’ām bə·šūḇ dā·wiḏ mê·hak·kō·wṯ ’eṯ- hap·pə·liš·tî wat·tê·ṣe·nāh han·nā·šîm mik·kāl ‘ā·rê yiś·rā·’êl lå̄·šūr wə·ham·mə·ḥō·lō·wṯ liq·raṯ šā·’ūl ham·me·leḵ bə·ṯup·pîm bə·śim·ḥāh ū·ḇə·šā·li·šîm
verses.literal: As the troops were returning home after David had killed the Philistine the women came out of all the cities of Israel to meet King Saul with singing and dancing with joyful songs and with tambourines and other instruments
verses.literalPt: Sucedeu, porém, que, vindo eles, quando Davi voltava de ferir os filisteus, as mulheres de todas as cidades de Israel saíram ao encontro do rei Saul, cantando e dançando, com adufes, com alegria, e com instrumentos de música.

verses.original: וַֽתַּעֲנֶ֛ינָה הַנָּשִׁ֥ים הַֽמְשַׂחֲק֖וֹת וַתֹּאמַ֑רְןָ הִכָּ֤ה שָׁאוּל֙ בְּאַלְפּוֹ וְדָוִ֖ד בְּרִבְבֹתָֽיו׃
verses.transliteration: wat·ta·‘ă·ne·nāh han·nā·šîm ham·śa·ḥă·qō·wṯ wat·tō·mar·nā hik·kāh šā·’ūl bə·ʾal·pō wə·ḏā·wiḏ bə·riḇ·ḇō·ṯāw
verses.literal: And as the women danced . . . they sang out Saul has slain his thousands and David his tens of thousands
verses.literalPt: E as mulheres dançando e cantando se respondiam umas às outras, dizendo: Saul feriu os seus milhares, porém, Davi os seus dez milhares.

verses.original: וַיִּ֨חַר לְשָׁא֜וּל מְאֹ֗ד וַיֵּ֤רַע בְּעֵינָיו֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר נָתְנ֤וּ לְדָוִד֙ רְבָב֔וֹת וְלִ֥י נָתְנ֖וּ הָאֲלָפִ֑ים וְע֥וֹד ל֖וֹ אַ֥ךְ הַמְּלוּכָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yi·ḥar lə·šā·’ūl mə·’ōḏ way·yê·ra‘ bə·‘ê·nāw had·dā·ḇār haz·zeh way·yō·mer nā·ṯə·nū lə·ḏā·wiḏ rə·ḇā·ḇō·wṯ wə·lî nā·ṯə·nū hā·’ă·lā·p̄îm wə·‘ō·wḏ lōw ’aḵ ham·mə·lū·ḵāh
verses.literal: And Saul was furious . . . and resented . . . this song They have ascribed tens of thousands to David he said but only thousands to me What more can he have but the kingdom
verses.literalPt: Então Saul se indignou muito, e aquela palavra pareceu mal aos seus olhos, e disse: Dez milhares deram a Davi, e a mim somente milhares; na verdade, que lhe falta, senão só o reino?

verses.original: וַיְהִ֥י שָׁא֖וּל עָוֹן אֶת־ דָּוִ֑ד מֵהַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וָהָֽלְאָה׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·hî šā·’ūl ʿå̄·wōn ’eṯ- dā·wiḏ mê·hay·yō·wm ha·hū wā·hā·lə·’āh
verses.literal: And from that day forward Saul kept a jealous eye on David
verses.literalPt: E, desde aquele dia em diante, Saul tinha Davi em suspeita.

verses.original: וַיְהִ֣י מִֽמָּחֳרָ֗ת וַתִּצְלַ֣ח רוּחַ֩ אֱלֹהִ֨ים׀ רָעָ֤ה׀ אֶל־ שָׁאוּל֙ וַיִּתְנַבֵּ֣א בְתוֹךְ־ הַבַּ֔יִת וְדָוִ֛ד מְנַגֵּ֥ן בְּיָד֖וֹ כְּי֣וֹם׀ בְּי֑וֹם וְהַחֲנִ֖ית בְּיַד־ שָׁאֽוּל׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî mim·mā·ḥo·rāṯ wat·tiṣ·laḥ rū·aḥ ’ĕ·lō·hîm rā·‘āh ’el- šā·’ūl way·yiṯ·nab·bê ḇə·ṯō·wḵ- hab·ba·yiṯ wə·ḏā·wiḏ mə·nag·gên bə·yā·ḏōw kə·yō·wm bə·yō·wm wə·ha·ḥă·nîṯ bə·yaḏ- šā·’ūl
verses.literal: The next day a spirit of distress sent from God came upon Saul and he prophesied inside the house while David played the harp as usual Now Saul was holding a spear . . .
verses.literalPt: E aconteceu no outro dia, que o mau espírito da parte de Deus se apoderou de Saul, e profetizava no meio da casa; e Davi tocava a harpa com a sua mão, como nos outros dias; Saul, porém, tinha na mão uma lança.

verses.original: וַיָּ֤טֶל שָׁאוּל֙ אֶֽת־ הַחֲנִ֔ית וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אַכֶּ֥ה בְדָוִ֖ד וּבַקִּ֑יר וַיִּסֹּ֥ב דָּוִ֛ד מִפָּנָ֖יו פַּעֲמָֽיִם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·ṭel šā·’ūl ’eṯ- ha·ḥă·nîṯ way·yō·mer ’ak·keh ḇə·ḏā·wiḏ ū·ḇaq·qîr way·yis·sōḇ dā·wiḏ mip·pā·nāw pa·‘ă·mā·yim
verses.literal: and he hurled it . . . thinking I will pin David to the wall But David eluded him twice
verses.literalPt: E Saul atirou com a lança, dizendo: Encravarei a Davi na parede. Porém Davi se desviou dele por duas vezes.

verses.original: וַיִּרָ֥א שָׁא֖וּל מִלִּפְנֵ֣י דָוִ֑ד כִּֽי־ הָיָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וּמֵעִ֥ם שָׁא֖וּל סָֽר׃
verses.transliteration: way·yi·rā šā·’ūl mil·lip̄·nê ḏā·wiḏ kî- hā·yāh Yah·weh ‘im·mōw ū·mê·‘im šā·’ūl sār
verses.literal: So Saul was afraid of David because the LORD was with David but had departed from Saul
verses.literalPt: E temia Saul a Davi, porque o SENHOR era com ele e se tinha retirado de Saul.

verses.original: וַיְסִרֵ֤הוּ שָׁאוּל֙ מֵֽעִמּ֔וֹ וַיְשִׂמֵ֥הוּ ל֖וֹ שַׂר־ אָ֑לֶף וַיֵּצֵ֥א וַיָּבֹ֖א לִפְנֵ֥י הָעָֽם׃פ
verses.transliteration: way·si·rê·hū šā·’ūl mê·‘im·mōw way·śi·mê·hū lōw śar- ’ā·lep̄ way·yê·ṣê way·yā·ḇō lip̄·nê hā·‘ām
verses.literal: Therefore Saul . . . sent David away and gave him command of a thousand men David led the troops out to battle and back . . .
verses.literalPt: Por isso Saul o desviou de si, e o pôs por capitão de mil; e saía e entrava diante do povo.

verses.original: וַיְהִ֥י דָוִ֛ד לְכָל־ דְּרָכָ֖ו מַשְׂכִּ֑יל וַֽיהוָ֖ה עִמּֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî ḏā·wiḏ lə·ḵāl də·rå̄·ḵå̄w maś·kîl Yah·weh ‘im·mōw
verses.literal: and he continued . . . to prosper in all his ways because the LORD was with him
verses.literalPt: E Davi se conduzia com prudência em todos os seus caminhos, e o SENHOR era com ele.

verses.original: וַיַּ֣רְא שָׁא֔וּל אֲשֶׁר־ ה֖וּא מַשְׂכִּ֣יל מְאֹ֑ד וַיָּ֖גָר מִפָּנָֽיו׃
verses.transliteration: way·yar šā·’ūl ’ă·šer- hū maś·kîl mə·’ōḏ way·yā·ḡār mip·pā·nāw
verses.literal: When Saul saw that David was very successful he was afraid of him
verses.literalPt: Vendo então Saul que tão prudentemente se conduzia, tinha receio dele.

verses.original: וְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וִיהוּדָ֔ה אֹהֵ֖ב אֶת־ דָּוִ֑ד כִּֽי־ ה֛וּא יוֹצֵ֥א וָבָ֖א לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃פ
verses.transliteration: wə·ḵāl yiś·rā·’êl wî·hū·ḏāh ’ō·hêḇ ’eṯ- dā·wiḏ kî- hū yō·w·ṣê wā·ḇā lip̄·nê·hem
verses.literal: But all Israel and Judah loved David because he was leading them out to battle and back
verses.literalPt: Porém todo o Israel e Judá amava a Davi, porquanto saía e entrava diante deles.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶל־ דָּוִ֗ד הִנֵּה֩ בִתִּ֨י הַגְּדוֹלָ֤ה מֵרַב֙ אֹתָהּ֙ אֶתֶּן־ לְךָ֣ לְאִשָּׁ֔ה אַ֚ךְ הֱיֵה־ לִּ֣י לְבֶן־ חַ֔יִל וְהִלָּחֵ֖ם מִלְחֲמ֣וֹת יְהוָ֑ה וְשָׁא֣וּל אָמַ֗ר אַל־ תְּהִ֤י יָדִי֙ בּ֔וֹ וּתְהִי־ ב֖וֹ יַד־ פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer šā·’ūl ’el- dā·wiḏ hin·nêh ḇit·tî hag·gə·ḏō·w·lāh mê·raḇ ’ō·ṯāh ’et·ten- lə·ḵā lə·’iš·šāh ’aḵ hĕ·yêh- lî lə·ḇen- ḥa·yil wə·hil·lā·ḥêm mil·ḥă·mō·wṯ Yah·weh wə·šā·’ūl ’ā·mar ’al- tə·hî yā·ḏî bōw ū·ṯə·hî- ḇōw yaḏ- pə·liš·tîm
verses.literal: Then Saul said to David Here is my older daughter Merab I will give her to you in marriage Only be valiant for me and fight the LORD’s battles But Saul was thinking I need not raise my hand against him let the hand of the Philistines be against him
verses.literalPt: Por isso Saul disse a Davi: Eis que Merabe, minha filha mais velha, te darei por mulher; sê-me somente filho valoroso, e guerreia as guerras do SENHOR (porque Saul dizia consigo: Não seja contra ele a minha mão, mas sim a dos filisteus).

verses.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־ שָׁא֗וּל מִ֤י אָֽנֹכִי֙ וּמִ֣י חַיַּ֔י מִשְׁפַּ֥חַת אָבִ֖י בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּֽי־ אֶהְיֶ֥ה חָתָ֖ן לַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer dā·wiḏ ’el- šā·’ūl mî ’ā·nō·ḵî ū·mî ḥay·yay miš·pa·ḥaṯ ’ā·ḇî bə·yiś·rā·’êl kî- ’eh·yeh ḥā·ṯān lam·me·leḵ
verses.literal: And David said to Saul Who am I and what is my family or my father’s clan in Israel that I should become the son-in-law of the king
verses.literalPt: Mas Davi disse a Saul: Quem sou eu, e qual é a minha vida e a família de meu pai em Israel, para vir a ser genro do rei?

verses.original: וַיְהִ֗י בְּעֵ֥ת תֵּ֛ת אֶת־ מֵרַ֥ב בַּת־ שָׁא֖וּל לְדָוִ֑ד וְהִ֧יא נִתְּנָ֛ה לְעַדְרִיאֵ֥ל הַמְּחֹלָתִ֖י לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî bə·‘êṯ têṯ ’eṯ- mê·raḇ baṯ- šā·’ūl lə·ḏā·wiḏ wə·hî nit·tə·nāh lə·‘aḏ·rî·’êl ham·mə·ḥō·lā·ṯî lə·’iš·šāh
verses.literal: So when it was time to give Saul’s daughter Merab to David she was given in marriage to Adriel of Meholah
verses.literalPt: Sucedeu, porém, que ao tempo que Merabe, filha de Saul, devia ser dada a Davi, ela foi dada por mulher a Adriel, meolatita.

verses.original: וַתֶּאֱהַ֛ב מִיכַ֥ל בַּת־ שָׁא֖וּל אֶת־ דָּוִ֑ד וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ לְשָׁא֔וּל וַיִּשַׁ֥ר הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינָֽיו׃
verses.transliteration: wat·te·’ĕ·haḇ mî·ḵal baṯ- šā·’ūl ’eṯ- dā·wiḏ way·yag·gi·ḏū lə·šā·’ūl way·yi·šar had·dā·ḇār bə·‘ê·nāw
verses.literal: Now Saul’s daughter Michal loved David and when this was reported to Saul it pleased him
verses.literalPt: Mas Mical, a outra filha de Saul amava a Davi; o que, sendo anunciado a Saul, pareceu isto bom aos seus olhos.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶתְּנֶ֤נָּה לּוֹ֙ וּתְהִי־ ל֣וֹ לְמוֹקֵ֔שׁ וּתְהִי־ ב֖וֹ יַד־ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל־ דָּוִ֔ד בִּשְׁתַּ֛יִם תִּתְחַתֵּ֥ן בִּ֖י הַיּֽוֹם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer šā·’ūl ’et·tə·nen·nāh lōw ū·ṯə·hî- lōw lə·mō·w·qêš ū·ṯə·hî- ḇōw yaḏ- pə·liš·tîm way·yō·mer šā·’ūl ’el- dā·wiḏ biš·ta·yim tiṯ·ḥat·tên bî hay·yō·wm
verses.literal: I will give her to David Saul thought so that she may be a snare to him and the hand of the Philistines may be against him So Saul said to David For a second time now you can be my son-in-law
verses.literalPt: E Saul disse: Eu lha darei, para que lhe sirva de laço, e para que a mão dos filisteus venha a ser contra ele. Pelo que Saul disse a Davi: Com a outra serás hoje meu genro.

verses.original: וַיְצַ֨ו שָׁא֜וּל אֶת־ עֲבָדָ֗ו דַּבְּר֨וּ אֶל־ דָּוִ֤ד בַּלָּט֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֨ה חָפֵ֤ץ בְּךָ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכָל־ עֲבָדָ֖יו אֲהֵב֑וּךָ וְעַתָּ֖ה הִתְחַתֵּ֥ן בַּמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.transliteration: way·ṣaw šā·’ūl ’eṯ- ʿă·ḇå̄·ḏå̄w dab·bə·rū ’el- dā·wiḏ bal·lāṭ lê·mōr hin·nêh ḥā·p̄êṣ bə·ḵā ham·me·leḵ wə·ḵāl ‘ă·ḇā·ḏāw ’ă·hê·ḇū·ḵā wə·‘at·tāh hiṯ·ḥat·tên bam·me·leḵ
verses.literal: Then Saul ordered his servants Speak to David privately and tell him Behold the king is pleased with you and all his servants love you Now therefore become his son-in-law
verses.literalPt: E Saul deu ordem aos seus servos: Falai em segredo a Davi, dizendo: Eis que o rei te está mui afeiçoado, e todos os seus servos te amam; agora, pois, consente em ser genro do rei.

verses.original: וַֽיְדַבְּר֞וּ עַבְדֵ֤י שָׁאוּל֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד הַֽנְקַלָּ֤ה בְעֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ הִתְחַתֵּ֣ן בַּמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאָנֹכִ֖י אִֽישׁ־ רָ֥שׁ וְנִקְלֶֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·ḏab·bə·rū ‘aḇ·ḏê šā·’ūl bə·’ā·zə·nê ḏā·wiḏ ’eṯ- had·də·ḇā·rîm hā·’êl·leh way·yō·mer dā·wiḏ han·qal·lāh ḇə·‘ê·nê·ḵem hiṯ·ḥat·tên bam·me·leḵ wə·’ā·nō·ḵî ’îš- rāš wə·niq·leh
verses.literal: But when Saul’s servants relayed . . . these words to David he replied Does it seem trivial in your sight to be the son-in-law of the king I am a poor man and lightly esteemed
verses.literalPt: E os servos de Saul falaram todas estas palavras aos ouvidos de Davi. Então disse Davi: Parece-vos pouco aos vossos olhos ser genro do rei, sendo eu homem pobre e desprezível?

verses.original: וַיַּגִּ֜דוּ עַבְדֵ֥י שָׁא֛וּל ל֖וֹ לֵאמֹ֑ר כַּדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה דִּבֶּ֥ר דָּוִֽד׃פ
verses.transliteration: way·yag·gi·ḏū ‘aḇ·ḏê šā·’ūl lōw lê·mōr kad·də·ḇā·rîm hā·’êl·leh dib·ber dā·wiḏ
verses.literal: And the servants told Saul what . . . David had said
verses.literalPt: E os servos de Saul lhe anunciaram isto, dizendo: Foram tais as palavras que falou Davi.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל כֹּֽה־ תֹאמְר֣וּ לְדָוִ֗ד אֵֽין־ חֵ֤פֶץ לַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ בְּמֹ֔הַר כִּ֗י בְּמֵאָה֙ עָרְל֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים לְהִנָּקֵ֖ם בְּאֹיְבֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְשָׁא֣וּל חָשַׁ֔ב לְהַפִּ֥יל אֶת־ דָּוִ֖ד בְּיַד־ פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer šā·’ūl kōh- ṯō·mə·rū lə·ḏā·wiḏ ’ên- ḥê·p̄eṣ lam·me·leḵ bə·mō·har kî bə·mê·’āh ‘ā·rə·lō·wṯ pə·liš·tîm lə·hin·nā·qêm bə·’ō·yə·ḇê ham·me·leḵ wə·šā·’ūl ḥā·šaḇ lə·hap·pîl ’eṯ- dā·wiḏ bə·yaḏ- pə·liš·tîm
verses.literal: Saul replied Say to David The king desires no other dowry but a hundred Philistine foreskins as revenge on his enemies But Saul intended to cause David’s death at the hands of the Philistines
verses.literalPt: Então disse Saul: Assim direis a Davi: O rei não tem necessidade de dote, senão de cem prepúcios de filisteus, para se tomar vingança dos inimigos do rei. Porquanto Saul tentava fazer cair a Davi pela mão dos filisteus.

verses.original: וַיַּגִּ֨דוּ עֲבָדָ֤יו לְדָוִד֙ אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וַיִּשַׁ֤ר הַדָּבָר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד לְהִתְחַתֵּ֖ן בַּמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְלֹ֥א מָלְא֖וּ הַיָּמִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: way·yag·gi·ḏū ‘ă·ḇā·ḏāw lə·ḏā·wiḏ ’eṯ- had·də·ḇā·rîm hā·’êl·leh way·yi·šar had·dā·ḇār bə·‘ê·nê ḏā·wiḏ lə·hiṯ·ḥat·tên bam·me·leḵ wə·lō mā·lə·’ū hay·yā·mîm
verses.literal: When the servants reported these terms to David he was pleased . . . . . . to become the king’s son-in-law Before the wedding day arrived
verses.literalPt: E anunciaram os seus servos estas palavras a Davi, e este negócio pareceu bem aos olhos de Davi, de que fosse genro do rei; porém ainda os dias não se haviam cumprido.

verses.original: וַיָּ֨קָם דָּוִ֜ד וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ׀ ה֣וּא וַאֲנָשָׁ֗יו וַיַּ֣ךְ בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּים֮ מָאתַ֣יִם אִישׁ֒ וַיָּבֵ֤א דָוִד֙ אֶת־ עָרְלֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם וַיְמַלְא֣וּם לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְהִתְחַתֵּ֖ן בַּמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּתֶּן־ ל֥וֹ שָׁא֛וּל אֶת־ מִיכַ֥ל בִּתּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yā·qām dā·wiḏ way·yê·leḵ hū wa·’ă·nā·šāw way·yaḵ bap·pə·liš·tîm mā·ṯa·yim ’îš way·yā·ḇê ḏā·wiḏ ’eṯ- ‘ā·rə·lō·ṯê·hem way·mal·’ūm lam·me·leḵ lə·hiṯ·ḥat·tên bam·me·leḵ way·yit·ten- lōw šā·’ūl ’eṯ- mî·ḵal bit·tōw lə·’iš·šāh
verses.literal: David and his men went out . . . and killed two hundred . . . Philistines He brought their foreskins and presented them as payment in full to become the king’s son-in-law Then Saul gave his daughter Michal to David in marriage
verses.literalPt: Então Davi se levantou, e partiu com os seus homens, e feriu dentre os filisteus duzentos homens, e Davi trouxe os seus prepúcios, e os entregou todos ao rei, para que fosse genro do rei; então Saul lhe deu por mulher a sua filha.

verses.original: וַיַּ֤רְא שָׁאוּל֙ וַיֵּ֔דַע כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עִם־ דָּוִ֑ד וּמִיכַ֥ל בַּת־ שָׁא֖וּל אֲהֵבַֽתְהוּ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yar šā·’ūl way·yê·ḏa‘ kî Yah·weh ‘im- dā·wiḏ ū·mî·ḵal baṯ- šā·’ūl ’ă·hê·ḇaṯ·hū
verses.literal: When Saul . . . realized that the LORD was with David and that his daughter Michal loved David
verses.literalPt: E viu Saul, e notou que o SENHOR era com Davi; e Mical, filha de Saul, o amava.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אסֶף שָׁא֗וּל לֵרֹ֛א מִפְּנֵ֥י דָוִ֖ד ע֑וֹד וַיְהִ֥י שָׁא֛וּל אֹיֵ֥ב אֶת־ דָּוִ֖ד כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yō·sep̄ šā·’ūl lê·rō mip·pə·nê ḏā·wiḏ ‘ō·wḏ way·hî šā·’ūl ’ō·yêḇ ’eṯ- dā·wiḏ kāl- hay·yā·mîm
verses.literal: he grew even more . . . afraid of David So from then on . . . Saul was David’s enemy
verses.literalPt: Então Saul temeu muito mais a Davi; e Saul foi todos os seus dias inimigo de Davi.

verses.original: וַיֵּצְא֖וּ שָׂרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיְהִ֣י׀ מִדֵּ֣י צֵאתָ֗ם שָׂכַ֤ל דָּוִד֙ מִכֹּל֙ עַבְדֵ֣י שָׁא֔וּל וַיִּיקַ֥ר שְׁמ֖וֹ מְאֹֽד׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yê·ṣə·’ū śā·rê p̄ə·liš·tîm way·hî mid·dê ṣê·ṯām śā·ḵal dā·wiḏ mik·kōl ‘aḇ·ḏê šā·’ūl way·yî·qar šə·mōw mə·’ōḏ
verses.literal: Every time . . . the Philistine . . . commanders came out for battle David was more successful than all of Saul’s officers so that his name was highly esteemed
verses.literalPt: E, saindo os príncipes dos filisteus à campanha, sucedia que Davi se conduzia com mais êxito do que todos os servos de Saul; portanto o seu nome era muito estimado.
